prompt.en: Explain why there is no single best investment for every family. State any three factors a family should weigh before deciding where to keep its money.

label.en: What the money is for and when it will be needed

level1.en: Think about the date the money has to be spent, not only about the return.

clue.en: Money needed in three months has no time to recover from a fall, while money needed after fifteen years does.

level2Template.en: The family should first decide what the money is for and ___ it will be needed.

label.en: The amount of risk the family is able to bear

level1.en: Could the family manage if part of this money disappeared for a year or two?

clue.en: A higher return is possible only by accepting a chance of loss, so the family must know how big a loss it can bear.

level2Template.en: It should also weigh the amount of ___ it is willing to take.

label.en: How quickly the money can be turned into cash

level1.en: If the money is needed without warning, which places can give it in cash, and which have to be sold first?

clue.en: Liquidity is how easily an asset becomes cash when needed, and money kept for an emergency has to be liquid.

level2Template.en: Finally, it should check how easily the money can be converted into ___ when needed.

eyebrow.en: Why there is no single best

text.en: Families differ in their goals, so the same option can be right for one and wrong for another.
The family should first decide what the money is for and ___ it will be needed.
It should also weigh the amount of ___ it is willing to take.
Finally, it should check how easily the money can be converted into ___ when needed.
